question: Conditional on how many stops a route-new species occupies, are those occupied stops more spatially clustered than expected under the existing activation nulls?
population: Frozen NAAMP matched pairs restricted to physically stable pairs with complete coordinates for all ten stops.

geometry.expected_span_k: For each route and k=2..10, enumerate all k-stop subsets and compute the mean maximum great-circle span. This is the route-specific random-k reference.
geometry.species_compactness: For each route-new species occupying k>=2 wet stops, 1 - observed_span/expected_span_k. Positive means more compact than a random k-stop subset on that route.
geometry.pair_total_compactness: Sum species_compactness over route-new multi-stop species; zero if none.
geometry.pair_mean_compactness: Mean species_compactness over route-new multi-stop species; zero if none.

model: Use the frozen matched-pair residualized rain design. Compare observed rain-contrast coefficients with 1,000 simulations from the kappa=2 uniform activation null and a=0.75 persistence-preserving null.
prefixed_diagnostic_rule: Cluster-density excess is supported if the observed pair_total_compactness coefficient is above the upper 95% bound under both nulls and pair_mean_compactness is above the upper 95% bound under both nulls.
interpretation: This is post-readback after the geographic-span analysis indicated compactness; it is diagnostic, not confirmatory.
A positive result supports dense local recruitment clusters conditional on occupied-stop count.
It does not identify whether clustering is caused by wetland complexes, local rainfall cells, habitat continuity or another mesoscale cue.
No individual movement or causal rainfall claim.
